'''Miles James''' "'''Deuce'''" '''McBride'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rende |first=Tom |title=Is Miles McBride’s Arrival Enough To Power The New York Knicks 2nd Unit? |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomrende/2024/03/31/is-miles-mcbrides-arrival-enough-to-power-the-new-york-knicks-2nd-unit/ |access-date=2025-03-04 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> (born September 8, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[New York Knicks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]].

McBride was selected with the 36th overall pick in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], but was traded to the Knicks on draft night. He won an NBA championship with the Knicks in [[2026 NBA Finals|2026]]. He plays both the [[Point guard|point]] and [[shooting guard]] positions.

==High school career==
McBride was a two-sport athlete at [[Moeller High School]] in [[Cincinnati|Cincinnati, Ohio]], playing basketball and [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]].<ref name="hertzel">{{cite web |last1=Hertzel |first1=Bob |title=Football experience paying off for McBride |url=https://www.register-herald.com/sports/college_sports/football-experience-paying-off-for-mcbride/article_73e7503b-6a4e-58f9-9831-262341956627.html |website=[[The Register-Herald]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=December 31, 2019}}</ref> He played alongside teammate [[Jaxson Hayes]] from 2015 to 2018. As a sophomore, he averaged 10.5 points, 2.5 assists, and 1.8 steals per game for the Division I state runners-up in basketball.<ref name=springer/> He suffered a season-ending left foot injury during a football game as a junior. McBride was sidelined from all but the final two games of the basketball season and helped Moeller win the Division I state title. He opted out of playing football in his senior season to focus on basketball.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Moeller's Miles McBride will not play football during his senior year |url=https://www.wcpo.com/news/insider/moellers-miles-mcbride-will-not-play-football-during-his-senior-year |website=[[WCPO-TV]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=April 23, 2018}}</ref> As a senior, McBride averaged 13.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game, leading Moeller to a 29–0 record and another Division I state championship.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=WVU's Bob Huggins: Miles 'Deuce' McBride of Moeller draws interest from next level |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/othercolleges/2020/10/23/bob-huggins-wvu-head-coach-miles-deuce-mcbride-moeller-high-school-draws-interest-next-level/3739813001/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=October 23, 2020}}</ref> His team achieved the first undefeated season in its division since 1995.<ref name="gresko">{{cite web |last1=Gresko |first1=Michael |title=Just call him "Deuce" |url=https://wvsportsnow.com/just-call-him-deuce/ |website=WV Sports Now |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=August 13, 2019}}</ref> A three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]].<ref name=springer>{{cite web |last1=Springer |first1=Scott |title=Moeller's McBride commits to West Virginia basketball |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2018/02/06/moellers-mcbride-commits-west-virginia-basketball/312823002/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=February 6, 2018}}</ref>

==College career==
On November 8, 2019, McBride made his debut for West Virginia, recording 11 points, six rebounds, four assists and four steals in a 94–84 win over [[Akron Zips men's basketball|Akron]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Justin |title=Miles McBride has stellar freshman debut as West Virginia downs Akron in opener |url=https://www.dominionpost.com/2019/11/08/miles-mcbride-has-stellar-freshman-debut-as-west-virginia-down-akron-in-opener/ |website=[[The Dominion Post (Morgantown)|The Dominion Post]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=November 8, 2019}}</ref> On December 29, he scored 21 points in a 67–59 win against [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].<ref>{{cite news |title=No. 22 West Virginia rallies, upsets No. 2 Ohio State 67–59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166136 |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 29, 2019}}</ref> On January 11, 2020, McBride scored a freshman season-high 22 points in a 66–54 victory over [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].<ref>{{cite web |title=McBride sparks West Virginia to victory over Texas Tech |url=https://www.statesman.com/sports/20200112/mcbride-sparks-west-virginia-to-victory-over-texas-tech |website=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=January 12, 2020}}</ref> As a freshman, McBride averaged 9.5 points and 2.4 rebounds per game while shooting 40.2 percent from the field, mostly coming off the bench.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nespor |first1=Cody |title=McBride Recognized as Recruiting Gem Following Freshman Season |url=https://wvsportsnow.com/mcbride-recognized-as-recruiting-gem-following-freshman-season/ |website=WV Sports Now |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=March 31, 2020}}</ref> He was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=WVU's Bob Huggins: Miles 'Deuce' McBride of Moeller draws interest from next level |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/othercolleges/2020/10/23/bob-huggins-wvu-head-coach-miles-deuce-mcbride-moeller-high-school-draws-interest-next-level/3739813001/ |website=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |accessdate=November 9, 2020 |date=October 23, 2020}}</ref>

In his sophomore season debut on November 25, 2020, McBride scored 23 points in a 79–71 win over [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Digby |first1=Matthew |title=McBride, McNeil tally career highs as Mountaineers hold off Jackrabbits in season opener |url=https://www.thedaonline.com/sports/mens_basketball/mcbride-mcneil-tally-career-highs-as-mountaineers-hold-off-jackrabbits-in-season-opener/article_55ea4410-2f90-11eb-b42f-6b1ff4d9e28d.html |website=[[The Daily Athenaeum]] |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 25, 2020}}</ref> On February 6, 2021, he posted 29 points, eight assists and seven rebounds in a 91–79 win against [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].<ref>{{cite web |title=No. 18 West Virginia cruises past No. 22 Kansas 91-79 in Big 12 tilt |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2021/02/06/mcbride-sherman-help-no-17-west-virginia-top-no-23-kansas/43376581/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=February 6, 2021}}</ref> In the first round of the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], McBride recorded a career-high 30 points, six rebounds and six assists in an 84–67 victory over [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Miles McBride scores 30, Bob Huggins gets win No. 900 for WVU |url=https://triblive.com/sports/miles-mcbride-scores-30-bob-huggins-gets-win-no-900-for-wvu/ |website=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=March 20, 2021}}</ref> As a sophomore, he averaged 15.9 points, 4.8 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game, earning Second Team All-Big 12 honors. On April 2, McBride declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. He later decided to remain in the draft, foregoing his college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=NBA Draft is an 'opportunity of a lifetime' for former Moeller basketball star Miles McBride |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/nba-draft-is-an-opportunity-of-a-lifetime-for-former-moeller-basketball-star-miles-mcbride |website=[[WCPO-TV]] |access-date=July 27, 2021 |date=July 14, 2021}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===New York Knicks (2021–present)===
McBride was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 36th pick by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] and then traded to the [[New York Knicks]], alongside [[Rokas Jokubaitis]], for [[Jeremiah Robinson-Earl]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Clark |first1=Dave |title=Miles McBride, WVU guard from Moeller HS, drafted 36th, traded from Thunder to Knicks |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/high-school/ohio-high-school/2021/07/29/miles-mcbride-2021-nba-draft-wvu-guard-moeller-hs-drafted-second-round-36th-new-york-knicks-thunder/5424035001/ |access-date=August 1, 2021 |work=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]] |date=July 29, 2021}}</ref> On August 6, 2021, the Knicks announced that they had signed McBride.<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Miles McBride|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-miles-mcbride|date=August 6, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=August 15, 2021}}</ref> Through the 2021 NBA Summer League, McBride averaged 15.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and 1.9 steals per game. He made his regular season debut on October 24.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bock|first=Ethan|date=2021-08-16|title=Deuce McBride Completes Summer League With 19 Points Against Hawks|url=https://wvsportsnow.com/deuce-mcbride-completes-summer-league-with-19-points-against-hawks/|access-date=2021-09-16|website=WV Sports Now}}</ref> On February 1, 2022, McBride was assigned to the [[Westchester Knicks]], and he scored 39 points in a 117–107 win over the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Priczak |first1=Chris |title=Miles McBride leads Westchester Knicks to 117-107 win over Delaware Blue Coats |url=https://www.postingandtoasting.com/2022/2/2/22913613/miles-mcbride-leads-westchester-knicks-to-117-107-win-over-delaware-blue-coats |website=Posting and Toasting |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=February 6, 2022 |date=February 2, 2022}}</ref>

On December 30, 2023, the Knicks announced they had signed McBride to a contract extension, which was reported to be for three years and $13 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-31 |title=Knicks' McBride agrees to 3-year, $13M extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39213194/miles-mcbride-agrees-3-year-13m-extension-knicks |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> With the trade of guards [[RJ Barrett]] and [[Immanuel Quickley]], a spot was cleared for McBride to be a permanent fixture in the Knicks rotation. On March 18, 2024, McBride started in place of an injured [[OG Anunoby]], recording a career–high 29 points, a career-high six three-pointers in a career-high 47 minutes as the Knicks defeated the [[2023–24 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] on the road, 119–112.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Knicks 119-112 Warriors (Mar 18, 2024) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585616 |access-date=2024-03-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> On March 23, McBride played in all 48 minutes of the Knicks' victory over the [[2023–24 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]], joining his teammate [[Josh Hart]] as the only players to not be subbed out of a game during the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kluska | first=Kenny | title=Second Knicks Player in Six Days Plays Entire 48 Minute Game | website=Last Word On Basketball | date=2024-03-24 | url=https://lastwordonsports.com/basketball/2024/03/24/second-knicks-player-in-six-days-plays-entire-48-minute-game-miles-mcbride/ | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref> In 68 games (14 starts) for the team, he averaged 8.3 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.7 assists, all of which were career-highs.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miles McBride 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431823/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

McBride made 64 appearances (including 10 starts) for New York in the [[2024–25 NBA season]], recording averages of 9.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2.9 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miles McBride 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431823/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On February 5, 2026, it was announced that McBride would be out indefinitely due to requiring surgery to repair a core muscle injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Knicks guard Miles McBride reportedly set for core muscle surgery, likely out until playoffs|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/breaking-news/article/knicks-guard-miles-mcbride-reportedly-set-for-core-muscle-surgery-likely-out-until-playoffs-182644936.html|access-date=March 4, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref> He played in 41 games (15 starts) for the Knicks in the regular season, averaging a career-high 12.0 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 2.6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miles McBride 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4431823/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> In Game 5 of the [[2026 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], McBride helped the Knicks achieve a 94–90 win and close out the NBA Finals against the [[San Antonio Spurs]], 4–1, securing the Knicks' first NBA championship in 53 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA championship|website=NBA.com|last=Lambert|first=Ben|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
McBride is the son of Walt and Kim McBride. His father played basketball for [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], while his mother played [[tennis]] for [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Ohio State]]. McBride's older brother, Trey, is playing basketball for the [[Itzehoe Eagles]] in Germany. He has been nicknamed "Deuce" since he was in third grade.<ref name="dyer">{{cite web |last1=Dyer |first1=Mike |title=Quarterback, basketball star Miles McBride is a true Man of Moeller |url=https://www.wcpo.com/sports/high-school-sports/ohio-high-school-sports/miles-mcbride-is-a-true-man-of-moeller |website=[[WCPO-TV]] |accessdate=November 8, 2020 |date=September 14, 2017}}</ref>
